name: RSA
quantum_impact: Broken by Shor's algorithm on a sufficiently capable cryptographically relevant quantum computer (CRQC).
recommended_hybrid: X25519+ML-KEM or RSA+ML-KEM hybrid key exchange
compatibility_notes: Widely supported; PQC migration requires protocol and library upgrades (e.g. TLS 1.3 hybrid groups).

name: RSA-1024
quantum_impact: Already considered classically weak (below 112-bit security) in addition to quantum vulnerability.
compatibility_notes: Should be retired regardless of quantum timeline.

name: RSA-2048
quantum_impact: Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm on a CRQC.
compatibility_notes: Common minimum baseline today; plan migration.

name: RSA-3072
quantum_impact: Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm on a CRQC.
compatibility_notes: Stronger classical margin, still quantum-vulnerable.

name: RSA-4096
quantum_impact: Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm on a CRQC.
compatibility_notes: Larger key does not mitigate quantum risk.

name: DSA
quantum_impact: Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm (discrete log variant).
recommended_hybrid: N/A - deprecate in favor of ML-DSA or hybrid ECDSA+ML-DSA
compatibility_notes: Largely deprecated already; prioritize replacement.

name: ECDSA
quantum_impact: Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm (elliptic curve discrete log).
compatibility_notes: Common in TLS certs and code signing.

name: ECDH
quantum_impact: Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm (elliptic curve discrete log).
compatibility_notes: Widely used in TLS 1.3; hybrid groups increasingly supported.

name: Diffie-Hellman
quantum_impact: Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm (discrete log).
compatibility_notes: Finite-field DH is being phased out in favor of ECDH/PQC.

name: Ed25519
quantum_impact: Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm (elliptic curve discrete log).
compatibility_notes: Modern default for SSH/signing; still quantum-vulnerable.

name: Ed448
quantum_impact: Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm (elliptic curve discrete log).
compatibility_notes: Less common; same quantum exposure as other ECC.

name: AES-128
quantum_impact: Grover's algorithm provides a quadratic speedup, roughly halving effective security margin (to ~64 bits equivalent search effort); not broken outright.
recommended_pqc: Not applicable (symmetric); consider AES-256 for larger quantum security margin.
compatibility_notes: Symmetric algorithms are not the primary PQC migration driver.

name: AES-192
quantum_impact: Grover's algorithm gives a quadratic speedup (~96-bit effective margin); not broken.
compatibility_notes: Adequate quantum margin for most use cases.

name: AES-256
quantum_impact: Grover's algorithm gives a quadratic speedup (~128-bit effective margin); considered quantum-resistant for practical purposes.
recommended_pqc: N/A - already considered quantum-resistant at this key size.
compatibility_notes: Recommended default for long-lived confidentiality needs.

name: AES-GCM
quantum_impact: Subject to the same Grover's-algorithm margin reduction as the underlying AES key size.
compatibility_notes: Prefer AES-256-GCM for long-lived data.

name: ChaCha20
quantum_impact: Grover's algorithm gives a quadratic speedup; considered quantum-resistant for practical purposes.
compatibility_notes: Common TLS 1.3 cipher, good quantum margin.

name: ChaCha20-Poly1305
quantum_impact: Same Grover's-algorithm consideration as ChaCha20.
compatibility_notes: Good quantum margin; the key establishment used alongside it is the higher-priority migration target.

name: DES
quantum_impact: Already classically broken (56-bit key); quantum considerations are secondary to its classical weakness.
recommended_pqc: N/A - retire immediately and replace with AES-256.
compatibility_notes: Should not be present in modern systems.

name: 3DES
quantum_impact: Deprecated by NIST for new use due to classical weaknesses (e.g. Sweet32); Grover's algorithm further reduces margin.
compatibility_notes: Legacy; retire where found.

name: MD5
quantum_impact: Already classically broken (collision attacks); not a quantum-specific concern.
recommended_pqc: N/A - replace with SHA-256 or SHA-3.
compatibility_notes: Must not be used for security purposes.

name: SHA-1
quantum_impact: Classically broken for collision resistance; Grover's algorithm affects preimage resistance quadratically.
recommended_pqc: N/A - replace with SHA-256 or SHA-3.
compatibility_notes: Deprecated by NIST; commonly still found in legacy certs/signatures.

name: SHA-224
quantum_impact: Grover's algorithm halves preimage-resistance exponent; collision resistance unaffected in the same way.
compatibility_notes: Consider SHA-256+ for new designs.

name: SHA-256
quantum_impact: Grover's algorithm gives a quadratic speedup on preimage search; still considered adequate.
compatibility_notes: Widely recommended default hash.

name: SHA-384
quantum_impact: Grover's algorithm consideration only; ample margin.
compatibility_notes: Good margin for long-lived integrity needs.

name: SHA-512
quantum_impact: Grover's algorithm consideration only; ample margin.
compatibility_notes: Good margin for long-lived integrity needs.

name: HMAC
quantum_impact: Security depends on the underlying hash; Grover's algorithm gives at most a quadratic speedup.
compatibility_notes: Ensure the underlying hash is SHA-256 or stronger, not MD5/SHA-1.

name: TLS 1.2
quantum_impact: Key exchange (RSA/ECDHE) is quantum-vulnerable; no standardized PQC hybrid support.
recommended_pqc: Upgrade to TLS 1.3 with PQC/hybrid key exchange groups.
compatibility_notes: Widely deployed; plan upgrade path to TLS 1.3.

name: TLS 1.3
quantum_impact: Default key exchange groups (X25519/ECDHE) remain quantum-vulnerable unless a PQC/hybrid group is negotiated.
recommended_pqc: Enable PQC/hybrid key-exchange groups (e.g. ML-KEM-based) per IETF drafts.
compatibility_notes: Best current baseline; add hybrid PQC groups as they standardize.

name: SSH
quantum_impact: Default key exchange (ECDH/DH) is quantum-vulnerable; some implementations support PQC/hybrid KEX (e.g. sntrup761x25519).
recommended_pqc: Enable PQC/hybrid SSH key exchange where the implementation supports it.
compatibility_notes: Check OpenSSH version for hybrid KEX support.

name: IPsec
quantum_impact: IKE key exchange is quantum-vulnerable; PQC extensions exist but are not universally deployed.
recommended_pqc: Adopt PQC-capable IKEv2 implementations as they mature.
recommended_hybrid: Hybrid IKEv2 key exchange where supported
compatibility_notes: Migration complexity depends heavily on vendor/appliance support.

name: HTTPS
quantum_impact: Inherits the quantum exposure of the underlying TLS configuration.
compatibility_notes: Ensure TLS termination points are upgraded, not just application code.

name: mTLS
quantum_impact: Both client and server certificates/key exchange inherit TLS's quantum exposure.
recommended_pqc: Plan PQC/hybrid certificates and key exchange for both endpoints.
recommended_hybrid: Hybrid certs (e.g. ECDSA+ML-DSA composite) as they standardize
compatibility_notes: Certificate rotation across many endpoints increases complexity.
